snippet.title: A Strategic Blueprint for AI Adoption in Accounting by Octavio Laos | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
AI adoption in accounting is no longer about experimenting with new tools. It is about solving real problems, changing workflows, and building measurable value across the firm.

In this Miles Masterclass course, A Strategic Blueprint for AI Adoption in Accounting, Octavio “OJ” Laos explores how accounting firms can move beyond AI buzzwords and build a practical, strategic approach to adoption.

The course begins with the evolution of AI, from big data and robotic process automation to generative AI, large language models, and natural language interfaces. OJ explains why this shift changes how professionals interact with software and why firms need to rethink roles, responsibilities, governance, and expectations.

The course also draws lessons from past technology shifts, including Bring Your Own Device and the move from Lotus Notes to Excel, to show how organizations adapt when new tools change everyday work. With AI, the pace is faster, making it essential for firms to balance opportunity with urgency, governance, training, and ROI tracking.

Learners will also explore how firms can structure and scale AI adoption using Modern Agile principles, digital teams, internal education programs, custom bots, and practical use cases across audit, billing, and cash flow forecasting.

Watch the full course to learn how accounting firms can build a strategic framework for AI adoption and turn AI from a disconnected experiment into a practical driver of transformation.

snippet.title: Beyond the AI Hype by John Higgins | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
AI has enormous potential for accounting firms, but success requires more than experimenting with new tools. It requires strategy, governance, measurement, and disciplined execution.

In this Miles Masterclass course, Beyond the AI Hype, John Higgins provides a practical roadmap for CPAs, CFOs, and advisory leaders who want to move beyond AI experimentation and build sustainable, measurable value from AI adoption.

The course begins by addressing the real barriers that prevent successful AI implementation. Rather than focusing on coding or model development, John explores the challenges of workflow integration, data governance, change management, and strategic alignment. Learners gain a clear understanding of why many AI initiatives fail and what separates successful adoption from costly experimentation.

The course also provides a practical overview of today’s AI landscape, including generative AI, agentic AI systems, and the future potential of artificial general intelligence. Through real-world case studies, John demonstrates how firms can avoid common mistakes and implement governance frameworks, acceptable use policies, validation processes, and human oversight mechanisms that turn AI from a risk into a business advantage.

The final modules introduce a five-pillar framework for AI adoption, covering objective setting, governance, pilot design, ROI measurement, and continuous improvement. Participants learn how to evaluate AI-enabled versus AI-native workflows, establish human-in-the-loop controls, and measure return on AI through productivity gains, reduced burnout, improved responsiveness, and operational efficiency.

Watch the full course to learn how accounting and finance leaders can deploy AI responsibly, measure its impact, and scale adoption without compromising quality, compliance, or professional judgment.

snippet.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act
snippet.description:
http://finacco.org/2025/06/05/2025-tax-reform/

On July 4, 2025, the President signed domestic spending and tax reform package referred to as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The Act represents the most significant update to the federal tax code since the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA).

The tax reform makes permanent many of the individual and business tax provisions passed in 2017 that were set to expire at the end of 2025. The legislation also introduces new, targeted tax breaks for seniors, workers and domestic business investment.

Certain tax provisions are effective January 1, 2025, while other items take effect in 2026.

Below are the major items in the 2025 tax reform.

Business tax provisions:

QBI deduction made permanent
100% bonus depreciation extended
Increase in Section 179 property expensing
Qualified production property deductions
Full local R&D expensing
Interest deduction relief
Excess Business Loss (EBL) limitation
International tax provisions:

FDII deduction is 33.34%, elimination of QBI adjustment
GILTI deduction is 40%, increase in FTC to 90%
BEAT rate is 10.5% (11.5% for certain banks)
Individual tax provisions:

SALT cap increased to $ 40 K
Additional $6,000 deduction for seniors
Permanent elimination of miscellaneous itemized deductions, personal exemption, etc.
Itemized deduction limit for high income earners
Estate and gift tax exemption is made permanent
Deduction for tips and overtime pay
Car loan interest deduction

snippet.title: AI in Construction: Solving for Field Reporting
snippet.description:
Logging and reporting field reports is a manual task for most construction companies. Here’s how AI can help.

This example is part part of our Built with AI series where I show real business examples of AI being used for daily work.

John, a construction manager needs to know how his construction crews are performing.

One of the ways he does this is by calculating how long his crews work, how much work they got done against how much they expected to get done when they priced the work.

It was a very manual process both in terms of inputting data and reporting back to his foreman on how the crews were performing.

This is how AI is now helping him:

The first thing we did is train them how to use Claude for Excel, which helps the construction manager get the information faster into the spreadsheet than manually doing it

Simple drag and drop to populate the fields and then a review that the fields were accurately updated. 

At the end of the week, he can now pull a report based on production rates.
But now we are in the process of automating it.

The company primarily runs ChatGPT business accounts with a few Claude licenses for finance and accounting. In this case we used Codex but you can also use Claude Code or Cowork.

Instead of dragging and dropping every single field log, at the end of the week all the field logs are automatically processed and put into the spreadsheet with a report that is developed so the construction manager can easily report on production rates to the field crews.

You may be wondering why we haven't built a skill yet both for the field processing and the report generation. We're just waiting for the company to fully standardise the output and how they feel processed. 

Those things are still in flux but once they do we'll definitely build the skill for it.

So now what has usually consumed hours every Friday for this construction manager has now become a less than an hour task.

This is just one way John is able to use AI to overcome the overwhelming at times amount of admin tasks his team has to do so they can focus on building rather than tedious paperwork.
